steps.text:
I added a built-in `flask config` command. It prints the app's configuration as JSON and masks the value of any key containing `SECRET`, `PASSWORD`, `TOKEN` or `KEY` as `"***"`.

The two new tests and the existing `routes` tests pass (8 passed), but only when run against this workspace's code. Plain `python -m pytest` imports a different Flask checkout (`C:\Users\LOQ\Coding\flask-3.1.3`), and there my two new tests fail because `config` isn't registered. I didn't run the full `tests/test_cli.py` with the workspace on the path.

In that unpatched run, 7 other tests also failed. They are `test_prepare_import` (6 cases) and `test_run_cert_path`, and they appear to be Windows drive-letter case mismatches (`C:` vs `c:`). I didn't touch them.

Changes:
- **`src/flask/cli.py`:** new `config_command`, registered in `FlaskGroup` next to `run`, `shell` and `routes`, so it shows up in `flask --help`. I also added `import json`. Values that can't be turned into JSON are printed as strings.
- **`tests/test_cli.py`:** `test_config_command_masks_secrets` and `test_config_command_in_help`.
- **`docs/cli.rst`:** a new "Show the Configuration" section, placed after "Debug Mode".

To verify, run `set PYTHONPATH=src&& python -m pytest tests/test_cli.py -q -k "config_command or routes"` (Windows `cmd` syntax). You can also run `flask --app <yourapp> config`.
